subtopic: Garbage Collection Mechanics and Memory Leak Profiling
question_text: What is the root cause of high Safepoint bias and extended 'Time To Safepoint' (TTSP) pauses in managed runtime garbage collectors?

options.text: Uncounted or long-running countable loops lacking safepoint poll checks preventing threads from halting promptly
Thread priority inversions in user space

answer_explanation: For a GC stop-the-world pause to occur, all threads must reach a safepoint. If a thread is executing a JIT-compiled loop that was optimized without safepoint polling checks, all other threads stall waiting.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: A. Rationale: For a GC stop-the-world pause to occur, all threads must reach a safepoint. If a thread is executing a JIT-compiled loop that was optimized without safepoint polling checks, all other threads stall waiting.
